summary: The revision is more honest. It drops dead keys, prices a one-off job as a one-off and names the demand gap as the riskiest assumption. The demand evidence has not changed: it is still AWS-only developer tool-lag issues. Each new filter narrows a segment that is still unsized, and Datadog shows GCP keys declining. Fund the 40-lead test, not the build.

objections.objection: Demand is still inferred. The revision keeps the same AWS-only developer issues, filed against upstream tools, and adds no buyer-side signal: no platform lead, auditor finding or consultancy describes in-use AWS-GCP or CI keys they would pay to remove. The concept admits this in risks[5] and riskiest_assumption.

Narrowing the segment shrank the market without sizing it. The target is now AWS-primary and GCP-secondary companies with 50-1,000 employees that use GitHub Actions, have a GCP org created before 3 May 2024, have a CSPM key finding open for months, and run no Vault or Teleport. Each filter cuts the count, and no estimate is given. With about $7.8k of first-year value and mostly one-off revenue, $10M ARR needs roughly 1,300 new logos every year. That is implausible from an unsized niche.

The problem is shrinking on the GCP half of the product. Datadog finds GCP service accounts with keys older than a year fell from 62% to 55% in a year. Google enforces key-creation blocking for every organisation created on or after 3 May 2024. Over half of old AWS keys are unused, which is hygiene and outside this product's scope. The pool of in-use, boundary-crossing keys may be only a handful per estate, and it gets smaller every year.

The easiest share of the target keys, static AWS/GCP keys in GitHub Actions, already has official step-by-step guides and maintained actions. Teams that have left those findings open for months may be showing low priority rather than lack of capacity. If so, they will defer a $6,000 fee too, until an audit forces the work.
objections.evidence: concept:pricing.rationale (one engineer-day per key is the concept's own estimate); concept:mvp.features[2]

objections.objection: WTP still rests on adjacent per-identity products. Nothing shows anyone paying a fixed fee for key-to-federation remediation, and consultancies may prefer to bill the hours themselves (open_questions[2]).

strongest_point: The riskiest-assumption test is well designed. A self-hosted report, filtered to in-use keys that the CSPM has left open, followed by an LOI or deposit, gives the cheap and direct buyer-side demand evidence that is missing today.
what_would_change_my_mind: At least 10 of the 40 contacted platform leads run the scanner, and the median report shows 10 or more in-use AWS-GCP or CI keys that a CSPM finding has left open for over 3 months.
At least 3 LOIs or 50% deposits at $6,000 within two weeks of the report review.
A bottom-up count (e.g. BigQuery/Vertex usage among AWS-primary firms from job postings or technographics) showing more than 3,000 qualifying companies.
At least one DevOps consultancy commits to reselling the fixed-price migration to 5 or more clients.

resolved_prior.objection: Cross-cloud need is assumed, not shown (all need statements AWS-only).
resolved_prior.note: Acknowledged and moved into risks and the riskiest assumption, but no new cross-cloud evidence was added.

resolved_prior.objection: Developer feature requests, some already fixed upstream, are not buyer purchase intent.
resolved_prior.note: The claims were reworded accurately and the RunPod item was dropped. The evidence is still developer tool-lag, with no buyer voice.

resolved_prior.objection: Prevalence is not budgeted pain; over half of old keys are unused.
resolved_prior.note: The product now scopes to in-use boundary-crossing keys and states the shrinking-problem risk. Whether enough such keys exist is still untested (objection 3).
The segment was narrowed further and sizing was deferred to an open question. The problem got worse, not better.

resolved_prior.objection: Demand is episodic, so subscription retention is weak.
resolved_prior.note: Pricing now matches the one-off job ($6,000 migration plus $150/month monitoring). The cost of this is a need for constant new logos, covered under objection 2.

resolved_prior.objection: WTP evidence from adjacent products; Vault price unverified.
resolved_prior.note: The Vault anchor was dropped and an LOI/deposit test was added, but no direct WTP evidence exists yet.
